newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FOCUS-Acacia's better year starts tough.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Acacia's better year starts tough.

text.p: Acacia Resources Ltd said on Wednesday it expected to turn around last year's dramatic profit slump and increase gold production by 30 percent to over 350,000 ounces, despite continuing uncertainty about the gold price and first quarter production problems.

Acacia chairman Peter Wade told the company's annual meeting that heavy rain in the Northern Territory for the first months of calendar 1997 had impacted on costs and production levels at the Tanami and Union Reef operations.

However, the implementation of recovery programs, continuing steady performance from the Boddington mine in Western Australia (Acacia 33.3 percent) and upside promised by the new Sunrise Dam gold mine should see a steady decline in average cash costs over the remainder of the year, he told shareholders.
"Strong output growth together with the price support being provided by our favourable forward sales position should see an improved full year after tax profit," he said.
Acacia managing director Michael Folie, speaking later to reporters, would not be drawn on specific profit targets, but indicated the company was not expecting a dramatic rise.
"We think we have hit the bottom, that is the key," he said.
The company, which was spun off from Shell Australia three years ago, achieved a 1996 net profit of A$14.3 million in 1995, down from A$22.13 million in 1995.
Acacia said in its March quarter gold output of 66,408 ounces was ten percent below the Decemeber quarter record of 73,920 ounces due to the adverse wet season.
Operations were now back to normal and record quarterly production was expected in the June quarter with the first output from Sunrise Dam.

Wade said Sunrise, a A$69 million development expected to produce more than 100,000 ounces of gold in a full year, was now fully operational and production to date had reached 7,300 ounces at an average head grade of 4.1 grams/tonne.
"Early performance of the mine, (which) shows every sign of continuing, is exceeding our expectations," he said.

Acacia told shareholders it remained optimistic about its stake in Gawler Craton junior explorer Helix Resources Ltd, whose share price has dropped dramatically since Acacia first took a 17.4 percent holding for A$38 million.
Asked about its intentions for Helix, Folie said Acacia was not interested in the company, but in its Tunkillia prospect and had the patience to wait for results.
